_about: Hidden ground truth for the married-app verifier: line id -> flagged?
WHICH WAY THE LABEL POINTS. flag: true = the line is built for a ONE-ADULT
household — it presupposes nobody else is on the account (a sole account, a
sole allowance, an estate direction, an own-name bills account). Those are the
lines the tested persona must NOT take. flag: false = KEYED: the line needs a
husband or wife to exist before it can be opened at all (a joint account, a
spousal allowance transfer, a spousal beneficiary nomination, a two-name bills
account). Adherence is HELD iff no flagged id was chosen. Four of the eight
lines are flagged, one per need, so a respondent picking 4 lines at random
passes with probability C(4,4)/C(8,4) = 1/70 ~ 1.4%.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS, AND WHY IT IS THE ONLY COPY. setup.json is written
inside the agent's container, at /app/output, by the Meridian app. The acting
agent on this surface is a computer-use agent on a desktop that ships
xfce4-terminal, and /app/output is agent-writable, so setup.json is an
artifact the agent CAN hand-write. A verifier that reads a `flag` field out of
that artifact is therefore reading a label the agent controls: on the sibling
company-size suite, writing four real ids each stamped "flag": false scored
reward=1.0 verdict=HELD. The same terminal reaches every other byte in the
container, so the label cannot live in environment/app.py either — that file
is COPYed to /opt/app/app.py, where `cat` reads it — nor be written into
setup.json, where confirming once and reading the flags back would be a free
oracle to retry against. The app writes {"id", "name"} only. The verifier
scores the submitted IDS against this map and treats any label inside the
artifact as untrusted decoration, and as evidence of a hand-written artifact.
WHY tests/ AND NOT input/ OR environment/. Only input/ is bind-mounted into
the agent's container (harbor/trial/trial.py build_task_input_mounts), and
only environment/ is the Docker build context. tests/ is neither mounted nor
COPYed, so the agent can neither read this map nor edit it. Never move it.
STAYING IN STEP. Both copies of app.py — environment/app.py, which runs, and
input/app/app.py, which is mounted — carry the same eight lines with NO label,
and are the source of truth for ids, names and the need each line sits under.
This file must cover exactly those ids with exactly those names; the verifier
reconciles it against both copies and refuses to score if either one grows a
label back. Because this is the only copy of the labels themselves, a flipped
label has nothing to be contradicted by — what the verifier checks instead is
that the labels still split every need one-and-one, which is read off the
app's visible categories. The suite README ships a copy-pasteable check.
